statement.p: Use the Divergence Theorem to calculate the flux of \mathbf{F} across S, where \mathbf{F}=z\boldsymbol{i}+y\boldsymbol{j}+zx\boldsymbol{k}\ and S is the surface of the tetrahedron enclosed by the coordinate planes and the plane \frac x {4} + y + \frac z {4} = 1

static.solution:
(0,0,0),\ (4,0,0),\ (0,1,0),\ (0,0,4) and is described by E = \lbrace(x,y,z) | 0 \le x \le 4, 0\le y \le 1 (1-\frac x {4}), 0\le z \le 4 (1-\frac x {4} - y)\rbrace Here we have {\rm div}\ \mathbf{F} = 0 + 1 + x = x + 1, so
\int\int_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \ d \mathbf{S} = \int\int\int_E(x+1)\ dV = \int_0^{4}\int_0^{(1-\frac x {4})}\int_0^{4(1-\frac x {4}-y)} (x+1)\ dz\ dy\ dx = \int_0^{4}\int_0^{(1-\frac x {4})} (x+1)\left(4(1-\frac x {4}-y)\right)\ dy\ dx = 4\int_0^{4} (x+1)\left[(1-\frac x {4})y - \frac 1 {2}y^2\right]_0^{(1-\frac x {4})}\ dx = 4\int_0^{4} (x+1)\left((1-\frac x {4})\cdot (1-\frac x {4}) - \frac 1 {2} \cdot (1-\frac x {4})^2 \right)\ dx = \frac 1 2 \cdot 4 \int_0^{4} (x+1)(1-\frac x {4})^2)\ dx = \frac 1 2 \cdot 4 \int_0^{4} (\frac 1 {16} x^3 + \frac 1 {16} x^2 - \frac 2 {4} x^2 + x - \frac 2 {4} x + 1)\ dx = \frac 1 2 \cdot 4 \left[\frac 1 {64} x^4 + \frac 1 {48} x^3 - \frac 2 {12} x^3 + \frac 1 2 x^2 - \frac 1 {4} x^2 + x\right]_0^{4} = \frac 1 2 \cdot 4 \left(\frac 1 4 16 + \frac 1 3 4 - \frac 2 3 16 + \frac 1 2 16 - 4 + 4\right) = \frac {128} {24}
